questions.q: Where were the Mole and the Rat coming back from at the start of the chapter?
choices: A long day's outing with Otter on the uplands
A long afternoon visit to Toad at Toad Hall
A night spent snug at the Badger's house
A shopping trip to the market in the town
questions.evidence: after a long day's outing with Otter

questions.q: What did the two animals do as they passed through the village?
choices: Looked in through the lit cottage windows
Knocked on cottage doors asking for food
Hid in a hedge from the barking village dogs
Bought supplies at the little village shop
questions.evidence: we can have a look at them through their windows if you like

questions.q: The animals watched the villagers with "something of wistfulness in their eyes." What does "wistfulness" mean?
choices: A sad, longing feeling
Angry, jealous feelings
Great fear and worry
Silly, giggling laughter
questions.evidence: something of wistfulness in their eyes

questions.q: What sense told the Mole that his old home was close by?
choices: His sense of smell
His sense of hearing
His sharp eyesight
His sense of touch
questions.evidence: I've just come across the smell of it

questions.q: Why did the Rat keep walking instead of stopping when the Mole first called to him?
choices: He was too far ahead to hear Mole's pain, and feared snow
He was angry with the Mole for dawdling behind him
He wanted to get home in time for a party at Toad Hall that night
He did not like the Mole's old home and would not go
questions.evidence: too far to catch the sharp note of painful appeal in his voice

questions.q: Why did the Mole follow the Rat instead of going to his home alone?
choices: His loyalty to his friend stood firm
He was too afraid of the dark to go alone
He had forgotten the way to his home
The Rat ordered him to come along at once
questions.evidence: his loyalty to his friend stood firm

questions.q: What happened when the two friends sat down to rest on some tree-stumps?
choices: The Mole broke down and cried about his lost home
The Rat fell fast asleep against a tree-stump
It began to snow very hard and fast
They met a group of field-mice with a lantern
questions.evidence: cried freely and helplessly and openly

questions.q: How did the Rat feel once he understood why the Mole was crying?
choices: Ashamed, calling himself a pig
Annoyed at the long delay in the cold
Amused, and laughed at the Mole
Too tired and cold to care much
questions.evidence: What a PIG I have been!

questions.q: What did the Rat decide to do after the Mole stopped crying?
choices: Go back and find Mole's home, even if it took all night
Hurry on home to the River Bank for a hot supper and bed
Go and ask the Badger to help them find the way
Build a shelter right there and wait for morning
questions.evidence: I'm going to find this place now, if I stay out all night

questions.q: What name was painted over the Mole's front door?
choices: Mole End
Mole Hall
Mole Cottage
The Burrow

questions.q: How did the Mole feel when he first looked around his dusty, neglected home?
choices: Miserable and sorry he had brought the Rat there
Proud and excited to show it off to the Rat
Angry that someone had broken in and stolen things
Calm, content and ready to go to bed
questions.evidence: why ever did I do it?

questions.q: How did the Rat help cheer the Mole up in his old house?
choices: He praised the house and kept them busy getting it ready
He told him to stop crying at once and go straight to bed
He took him straight back to the River Bank that night
He invited Toad and the Otter to come for supper
questions.evidence: What a capital little house this is!

questions.q: What food did the friends find when they foraged in the Mole's cupboards?
choices: Sardines, captain's biscuits and a German sausage
Bread, butter, honey and a jar of plum jam
Cold chicken, a ham and a pork pie
Apples, nuts and a big fruit cake
questions.evidence: a tin of sardines--a box of captain's biscuits, nearly full--and a German sausage

questions.q: Who arrived outside Mole End while the friends were about to eat?
choices: Field-mice who had come carol-singing
The Otter and the Badger, wet with snow
Weasels from the Wild Wood looking for trouble
The hedgehog children, lost on their way home
questions.evidence: They go round carol-singing regularly at this time of the year.

questions.q: What did the Rat do so there would be enough supper for the field-mice?
choices: He sent a field-mouse with the lantern to buy food
He cut the German sausage into tiny bits for everyone
He went out to the village shops himself in the snow
He asked the field-mice to fetch food from their homes
questions.evidence: the field-mouse was provided with an ample basket for his purchases

questions.q: What happened when the Mole asked a field-mouse to recite part of last year's play?
choices: He was so shy he could not say a word
He gave a wonderful, loud performance
He sang a long carol instead
He ran out of the house in fright

questions.q: The Mole's old room received him back "without rancour." What does "rancour" mean?
choices: Bitter, angry feelings
Loud, rattling noise
Bright, glaring light
Cold, damp air from outside
questions.evidence: smilingly received him back, without rancour

questions.q: What does the Mole come to understand at the end of the chapter?
choices: He'll go back to his new life, but it's good to have a home
He must give up the river and stay at Mole End forever after
His old home is worthless and he should sell it soon
He wants to move in with the field-mice in the village
questions.evidence: it was good to think he had this to come back to
